english:
My name is Nandana. I am from Pala. This is my father, mother, and younger brother. My younger brother is studying in 10th standard.
The first time I took the Covenant here was on the 27th date, in 27, 7, 2025. That is when I first took the Covenant here.
It was Mother Mary who brought me to this place—Mother Mary herself brought me here. In this holy place filled with the living presence of Jesus and Mother Mary, where Mother Mary appeared,
I thank God very much for giving me the grace to give my testimony today. To glorify the name of Jesus, I first of all offer my testimony to Jesus and Mother Mary.
The situation that led me to take the Covenant is this: I studied TTC for two years. During that time, in my very first attempt,
I wrote and attended the KTET exam—KTET is the Kerala Teacher Eligibility Test. Only if we pass this test can we get a teaching job.
Along with me, there were 16 people studying. In the first attempt itself, 14 people passed KTET. Then two people did not pass—one of them was me.
After that, next time also I tried once again and wrote the exam, but I was not able to pass the exam.
When I was sitting in sadness like that, I watched the Covenant meditation of our respected Fr. VP Joseph on the phone.
And that is how I came to know about Mother of Kreupasanam, and came to this place, and here I took the Covenant. I took the Covenant here.
After taking the Covenant, if we follow the Covenant conditions, Mother told the disciples of Jesus: “Do whatever He tells you.” That means, if we keep those conditions and do accordingly, Jesus will surely intervene in our life.
As it is said there, we are Non-christians, but we do attend Holy Mass on Sundays. We will never miss Holy Mass on Sundays.
No matter what fever we have, no matter what sickness we have, not even one Sunday we missed Holy Mass. Because Holy Mass is Lord's day.
Sunday is the day when Jesus comes close to us. It is an obligatory day. In the Holy Mass, the birth of Jesus, the crucifixion of Jesus, the resurrection of Jesus, and through that, Jesus gives us the Holy Spirit—this is what happens in the Holy Mass.
It is Jesus who has given us the Holy Spirit. So, Jesus gave His own life as the sacrifice of atonement for our sins.
There is a verse in the Gospel: John 1:1 — “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Through that Word,
our Heavenly Father has given everything to all of us through Jesus. And the crucifixion of Jesus is present for us here itself. Our Jesus—our Mother—accepted death on the Cross.
When we look at that, we can understand that the problems in our life are nothing.
We do not experience even one percent of the pain that God experienced. In our pain we think, “O God, why has such great suffering come only to us?” We break down completely.
But when we remember the crucifixion of Jesus, we understand that in our life, God has not given us a suffering as great as that.
The patience God has given us is nothing else but a sign of how much God loves us. When suffering comes, only then do we think about God.
When I did not get it in my exam, that is when I searched for God. When that suffering came, I began to seek God.
And I discovered that the true God is Jesus. We are non-Christians, and that is why we searched for Jesus.
When we came to this place, we firmly believed that Jesus and Mother Mary are truly the one true God.
Jesus has said: “To those who believe in His Word, He gave the power to become children of God.” We firmly believed that Word. This time—on September 18—was my KTET exam. It was the fourth time I wrote it.
Trusting in Jesus, and seeking the intercession of Mother Mary, this was the fourth time I wrote it. Only I was left to pass this exam.
So I told Mother Mary, “Mother, let me pass the exam this time, because when I give the Kreupasanam magazine to someone else, my own life must be a testimony.”
So I prayed to Mother Mary: “Mother, make me a witness to the apparition.” That is how I prayed.
This time, after I wrote the exam, when the result was supposed to come, I prayed to God: “Lord, the exam ended on September 18, and after that I had no news.” Everyone asked,
“Did the result come? Did you pass the exam? It has been so many days—why hasn’t the result come yet?” they asked.
That is when I remembered and said, “God, the result still has not come.” And if we want a job, we must pass the KTET exam to be able to apply to schools.
Then I said to Mother Mary, “Mother, December is your birthday. Before December 8, let me know my exam result.” I prayed by fixing December 8 as the date.
On December 6, Mother Mary gave me a happy message. It was in the evening of that day.
I came to know about it that day. A friend of mine called me and asked, “Hey, did the result come? Did you check?” I said,
“I didn’t see anything in the newspaper or on TV,” because it was election time, so the KTET result announcement had not come in the news.
Then I said, “Is it?” At that time I was in Pala. That day I had come to pray near Mother Mary, at the church of the Cross.
So I said, “Let me go home and check.” I didn’t know. After coming home, I checked.
Before that itself, I told Mother Mary: “Mother, whether I fail or pass the exam, I will not leave you. Let whatever is your will be fulfilled.” Then I prayed.
I recited the Creed, and also recited the apparition prayer of Mother Mary. Then I logged in and opened that website.
When I opened and checked, I only needed around 80 marks to pass. God gave me more than that and made me pass the exam this time.
So, this year I passed KTET. Mother Mary made me an instrument—a witness—for the apparition.
So I gave my testimony, and my life itself became a testimony. I began giving the magazine to others, and using the holy oil. I shared my testimony—my life testimony itself—with others.
I told them: even if you have sickness or afflictions, even for exams— now many people are waiting to write IELTS, to go to Germany, and so many things, right?
They will say, “I wrote once or twice but didn’t get it. I took the Covenant but nothing happened.”
To such people I have only one answer to say: our life does not go according to what we decide. We decide something, but God thinks differently.
God thinks, works, and acts differently. Our life will never go exactly as we imagine.
God knows when and what to give us. Trust in God. Then God will give it to us at the right time.
That is what I want to say through my testimony. Because God will fulfill each and every plan, but not for our destruction—rather, for our good and for our prosperity.
God knows when He should give it to us. So that was my first intention—Mother of God made me a witness in that. The second thing is: we did not have a good house.
The house we had—if I should say it—was like a circus tent. Because it was not a proper house. Even when it rained, all the water would come inside the house.
So yes, we like the rain, but when it rains, we feel afraid to lie down and sleep, because all the water keeps dripping from the roof.
So like that I prayed to Mother Mary: “Mother, we do not have a good house. Mother Mary, please build a good house for us,” I said. Around that time, under the Life Mission project, we submitted an application for a house.
After that, there was no further news. We had only submitted the application. Then my mother was here, sweeping the yard.
At that time, my mother’s younger sister called on phone. In my mother’s family, everyone has a good house—only we did not have a good house like that.
So my mother said, “Everyone has a good house, but I don’t have a home.” Then my aunt said, “Don’t you have Mother Mary, the Kreupasanam Mother?
You will get a house. Hasn’t Mother done everything for you?” she asked. After saying that, she ended the call.
My mother cried and prayed to Kreupasanam Mother: “Mother, give me a good house. Let me enter and live in it one day. And the next day, call me—I will come joyfully with Mother Mary,” she said.
At that moment, my mother cried. Then she called my uncle for a need. That is, if something at home runs out—like tea powder or something—my mother immediately calls my uncle.
When she called my uncle, the phone was busy—his number was busy. Then my mother continued the next work.
After that, my uncle called back and said: “Dear, the officers from the Panchayat called. The loan for our house has been approved. They said to come to the Panchayat tomorrow itself and bring all the documents.”
Hearing that, my mother did not know whether she was feeling great joy or great emotion. At that very moment my mother cried and prayed to Mother Mary: “Mother,
I just told you only now. And in that same moment, Mother made it happen and got it approved,” is what I can say.
Then we submitted all the documents for the house construction. After that, Mother built the house for us. Because, when we looked at the house plan,
Mother herself redesigned it again. We desired only a small house, but when it was built, it became a well-facilitated house.
We had only two and a half cents of land, but on that land, Mother Mary built us a house with good facilities. In this way, Mother Mary again made us an instrument of the apparition.
That is what I say as the second testimony. The third testimony is this: My mother asked many of the women in the Kudumbashree, “Can I join this?” But none of them included her.
So my mother herself decided: “I will step forward—we will form a Kudumbashree group.” So my mother went for that,
and told everyone about Kudumbashree and its need—saying, “We should gather in Kudumbashree.” She asked to only 10 people, but the number of people who came were 30.
Somehow she brought them together.
After that, those 30 women in the Kudumbashree group—later, each person began to state different needs and matters, and some people left. Still, 20 people remained.
Now, among those who come, many are families with government jobs, money, and wealth. But we did not have money—we were an ordinary family.
So if we asked for a loan, they would not give it. They asked, “If we give them a loan, how will they repay it? What confidence can we give it on?” That is what they asked.
My mother brought Kudumbashree together, but when the matter of giving a loan came, they asked, “How can we trust them and give?” So they did not give the loan.
During the Corona period, we suffered a lot. After that, all these people used to insult us, because even inside Kudumbashree there were many dishonest things. So my mother asked—because we know,
In Kudumbashree there are positions like secretary and president.
We have members, and we have to deposit the members’ money in the bank. We should not keep it in hand.
When my mother saw such dishonesty, she asked just one question. But because of that question, later everyone blamed my mother.
When Kudumbashree meetings happened, they would not allow my mother to enter that place. So there were many difficulties and situations like that. They would not accept the money my mother gave.
But we deposited it properly and regularly in the bank. And after that, they themselves filed a case against us.
When senior officials came and questioned it, they asked: “For what reason should they be removed? Or why should they be expelled from Kudumbashree?” There was no reason.
Even if they did not take our money, we still deposited it properly. If they asked for another reason—there was none. We were just an ordinary family.
So all of them stood against us. But because God is on the side of the righteous, victory was on our side. The people who tried to expel us—the senior officials from the Panchayat removed them,
saying, “We do not need such a Kudumbashree here anymore.” That is what I call the third testimony. Because even if we do any work sincerely, God is with us.
Because God is righteous. God is with the side of the righteous. God will never stand with cheating and deception. Likewise, the fourth testimony is this: When people accuse me, I get hurt quickly.
If someone says something that troubles me—whether they are friends or family members— I get upset immediately.
But I do not react. I come home, sit alone, and cry. I look to God and ask, “God, don’t You see what is happening to me?” I tell everything to God.
When I come home, I may tell my uncle or my mother, but I would speak more to God.
But because I remained calm, and even though I passed through suffering with patience, it is God Himself who has brought me to this stage.
Until today I have never gone up on a stage. I am someone who has never stepped onto a stage. But today, I have come here to Mother’s presence to give testimony for God.
God made me a witness. He entrusted me to give testimony in such a holy place.
So in my testimony, I have only one thing to tell everyone— to all the devotees who have taken the Covenant: After taking the Covenant, we must seek God.
We must seek the Kingdom of God. We should not give importance to our missions— not to our worldly goals. That is not what we should run after. We must seek God. God gives us the Holy Mass. Through the Holy Mass, Jesus comes. So we must seek God.
God will give us the remaining things, because everything is in God’s hands. It is said in John 1:1: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”
That Word—God, our Heavenly Father—has given everything to us through Jesus. He has given us all things.
Now it is we who must act. Now, whatever responsibilities and duties we have, we must do them sincerely, and we must do them for the glory of God’s name.
Then surely Mother Mary and Jesus will make us also witnesses of the apparition, and will bless us by giving us the grace to proclaim the Covenant in this holy place.
That is what I want to tell everyone. If I speak about the missionary work I have done: I take the Kreupasanam magazines from here. I make the sign of the Cross on it with the holy oil I received here.
I recite the Creed. I share my life experience with everyone. And I give the magazine to everyone.
Then, some people do not know how to read. So I read it out to them. I read out the testimonies—the testimonies in the Kreupasanam magazine.
I tell them: “You must believe this. These are the life experiences of each person, what they are saying—so you must believe it.” And then, we must trust in God even more.
When we come to this holy place called Kreupasanam, we will be able to see God. No matter what, you should go to Kreupasanam and take the Covenant.
Mother Mary will accomplish all your intentions, that is what I say. Works of charity: My mother and I prepare 10 packets of food (meals) from home,
and on every First Friday, many people come to the church here. We give food to those who struggle to get food.
And we do not ignore even one person who stretches out a hand before us. Whatever we have in our hands, we give there.
For example, last time my mother and I went to Pala, to the church of the Cross. If we have 500 rupees in hand, we give 300 to those who ask.
Because we know— Mother Mary and Jesus come close to us in many forms. It may be as a hungry person, or it may be as an ordinary person,
Sometimes they may be ordinary workers who sell candles. When they ask for even ten rupee, we give thirty rupee, because I believe that God is present among the poor.
God comes in many forms—we do not know in what way He will come. So, believing that it is God, I give that money to God Himself.
At that moment, when I give money to that person, I say: “Lord, may Your name be glorified.” “To the person stretching out a hand before me,
whether it is ten rupees or whatever I am able to give—whatever I have in my hand, I will give.” And I say,
“May my God’s name be glorified.” In this way I do missionary work.
Also, near my place there are children in a special school. I give them clothes—good clothes.
Now, after taking the Covenant, my interest in fancy dresses with stones and flowers has reduced. Now I have the most interest in simple, light dresses.
So I gave all those good clothes to those children. At that time I said, “Mother, Mother Mary, for the glory of Jesus’ name, here—I have given this to the children.”
When we see those children, we feel sorrow. Then we remember how blessed we are—how fortunate we are.
And we give thanks—many thanks—to Jesus and Mother Mary.

the daughter, as a witness of the apparition—together with her family—has taken the Covenant, and today this Christian family is standing here at this altar.
As Nandana said, I have never gone anywhere for a stage performance.
But today, in the presence of the Blessed Mother, I have received a great opportunity to stand here as a witness of this apparition. I consider it a great blessing. The main purpose for which this daughter came to take the Covenant,
They did not have a house. On just two and a half cents of land, Jesus quickly blessed them with a good home. When they took and renewed the Covenant, the Life Mission loan was sanctioned, and they received a good house.
She also testified that in the KTET exam, the Blessed Mother granted the daughter a great victory.
In every life situation and in every sorrow, the Blessed Mother gave her closeness and strong support.
Nandana was also able to understand that the Blessed Mother gives the “green signal” for all matters through Jesus.
And today, Nandana and her family are able to live a life guided by God’s call—rising from a truly Christian way of life.
In the loneliness and struggles of their life, without breaking down, they were able to take good things from every situation, and connect it with how Jesus suffered.
We can understand that this family and this daughter have received a great spiritual holiness. This is a testimony that makes us reflect on where we stand.
Is it my worldly needs that matter most, or is my God—my Jesus—my Savior? This is a testimony that makes us examine and decide that.
By weighing our own sorrows and our spiritual growth, we can unite ourselves with this testimony and entrust all our sorrows to the Blessed Mother.
Praying for the great blessing to live with holiness, and thanking God for all the blessings and goodness this family has received,
let us give a big round of applause. May the Blessed Mother raise all of us too as witnesses of this apparition.
